title: ISA029 Sigattukara Hong 321.6
about: All computer programming is basically question asking, rather than choice making.
credits: Over the course of a day, ScorsBT4 listened to the world, gathering 365 moments of radio from anywhere on the dial: shortwave, FM and internet stations, open microphones, hydrophones in the sea, the earth's own natural radio and old recordings from the Internet Archive. The sounds were placed by a score of curves and points after John Cage's "Fontana Mix", and the dice decided the rest. 85 of those moments are in these songs.

This was a truly random day, as about one day in seven is: all day the algorithm kept everything, static and silence included, matched nothing for beauty, and asked no song to go anywhere. Nothing was discerned, classified, or judged.

This album is impermanent. The broadcasts collected are gone. The recordings it gathered were thrown away once it was made. Tomorrow it will be replaced by another, which will never be heard again either. Each day the chance that it is the last grows: today's was 1 in 337, tomorrow's is 1 in 336. It exists for a day. Listen while it's here. More info on the project.
